gen-nixie-one-gf-telex: Nixie One draws thin-looking letters with a stroke that never swells, a nostalgic, retro-tech voice. Telex follows with curvy, unclamped forms, and the two feel like an old terminal manual that learned to relax.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tenor-sans: Hairline strokes that hold one width around every curve give Nixie One its retro-tech edge. Tenor Sans sits beside it as a contemporary sans, its thick strokes only slightly heavier than thin, so a larger heading size lets the delicate top face breathe.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tirra: Nostalgic and a bit retro-tech, Nixie One looks cut from strips of equal width. Tirra, a plain sans with round forms like open parentheses, takes over below, so a heading well above the body size keeps the two distinct.
gen-nixie-one-gf-titillium-web: Nostalgic, with open curves and a stroke that never swells like a brush, Nixie One sets the tone up top. Titillium Web, a sans-serif with stroke ends set far apart, would read as approachable and modern across a long passage.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tomorrow: Nostalgic and retro-tech, Nixie One is best at holding a constant pen pressure through open curves at display size. And Tomorrow, a plain sans, does its best work lower down, with bowls opening like a cupped palm of clay.
gen-nixie-one-gf-trispace: Trispace spreads sparse, widely set letters whose curves open outward, sitting beneath the single-stylus line of Nixie One. Its strongest quality is that spacious, approachable quiet.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Nostalgic and retro-tech, Nixie One traces open curves at a constant width, while Tsukimi Rounded adds round forms like open parentheses with parallel edges. Both stay light and clear.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tuffy: Tuffy looks pencil-sketched, never pressing harder, with a widely parted s. Made small, Nixie One would lose its hairline charm, while a large Tuffy sans would crowd it out.
gen-nixie-one-gf-urbanist: Retro lines, modern manners. Nixie One keeps open curves at a constant width, and Urbanist follows with a broad-nibbed, rolling-ball stroke that never curls shut, so the page moves from old tech to now.
gen-nixie-one-gf-varela: Nostalgic from the first curve, Nixie One keeps a constant stroke and open, gapped shapes in its display lines. Varela, a plain sans with a wide-mouthed c, handles the everyday text.
